title: "Improve Engagement" Is Not a Success Metric
description:
Every PRD needs its own success metric, and "improve engagement" isn't one. This Short walks the four-question checklist from the Product Manager Mastery Path: can you measure it with existing instrumentation, is there a clear baseline, does it plausibly move the North Star, and is the target specific and numeric? We anchor it with the lesson's worked example: a project-management SaaS whose weekly-digest-email initiative set the target "+8 percentage points in week-3 team retention within 6 weeks of launch, against the current 35% baseline."

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/07-metrics-kpis-basics/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Improve engagement is not a success metric. If nobody can check whether you actually hit it, it doesn't belong in your PRD.

display.heading: "Improve engagement" is not a success metric

beats.narration: Every PRD needs its own success metric, separate from the North Star. Run it through a checklist. Can you measure it with the instrumentation you already have? Is there a clear baseline before launch?

display.heading: Every PRD needs its own success metric
display.subheading: Measurable with existing instrumentation? Clear baseline before launch?

beats.narration: Without a baseline, improvement is unfalsifiable. Then: does moving this metric plausibly move the North Star, so you're not chasing a vanity number? And is the target specific and numeric?

display.heading: Does it move the North Star -- or just a vanity metric?
display.subheading: "Improve engagement" isn't checkable. "+10% week-2 retention" is.

beats.narration: Here's the lesson's real example. A project-management SaaS ships a weekly digest email. Its success metric: plus eight points in week-three team retention, within six weeks of launch, against the current thirty-five percent baseline.

display.heading: The weekly-digest-email initiative
display.subheading: "+8 points in week-3 team retention within 6 weeks, vs. the current 35% baseline"

beats.narration: That's leading, specific, and measurable, and it ties straight back to the North Star. Full lesson's linked below.
